heading: ཚོགས་ཞིང་སྤྱན་འདྲེན་པ།

From the supreme realm of Potala,
Born from the green syllable TĀṂ,
Liberating transmigrating beings through the light of the syllable TĀṂ,
I invite the green Tārā together with her retinue of twenty-one.

With the crowns of gods and demigods,
Bowing down before your lotus feet,
To her who liberates from all misfortune,
Homage to the Mother Tārā.

And their various levels of mental capacity,
I pray that you turn the wheel of Dharma of the Great Vehicle—the Bodhisattva vehicle of both Sūtra and Mantra—the Small Vehicle—the two vehicles of Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas—and the Common Vehicle—the two vehicles of gods and humans of the higher realms.

heading: དྲུག་པ་སྐུ་མྱ་ངན་ལས་མི་འདའ་བར་གསོལ་བ་འདེབས་པའི་ཡན་ལག
translation:
Until saṃsāra is emptied,
Do not pass into nirvana, but through your compassion,
I pray that you look upon all sentient beings
Who are sinking in the ocean of suffering.

Thus, having attained the enlightenment in which all the merit of these three—accumulation, purification, and increase—is ultimately merged as one with the wisdom mind of the Jetsunma, the aspiration to accomplish the benefit of others together with you in the interim is:

heading: བདུན་པ་བསྔོ་སྨོན་ཡན་ལག
translation:
Whatever merit I have accumulated,
May it all become the cause for enlightenment in which my mind is merged as one with the Jetsunma,

translation: *Oṃ* is the introductory syllable. Because she has become the supreme mother of all the victorious ones, the Venerable Lady is exalted above the level of ordinary beings, and thus she is the Noble Lady (*Ārya*). Because she liberates those who have faith from cyclic existence, the lower realms, and fears, she is the Savior (*Tārā*); thus, "Homage to Tārā." This is the translator's homage. To whom is the homage paid? *Tāre* is the Savior; because she accomplishes [tasks] in an instant or in a single day, she is the Heroine who is swifter in her enlightened activity than other deities and who quickly turns back obstacles. *Tuttāre* is she who dispels fears. *Ture* is the Savior who grants all benefits—one's own, others', and the ultimate goal. The syllable *Svāhā* means "I bow to you." It appears that this is a blessed [verse] that arose in the manner of a summary of Tārā, which is renowned as having been supplemented from other tantras by the glorious Jowo Rje and others.

heading: གཉིས་པ་བསྟོད་པ་དངོས།
translation: To whom is the homage paid? It is to that Savior who, through her wisdom, liberates those with faith from all fears; who, out of love for the one offering praise, does not delay even for an instant in her enlightened activity, and is thus the "Swift" one of compassion; and who, being capable, is the "Heroine" because she is certain of her ability to protect from all the fears of cyclic existence and peace. In her wrathful aspect, her wisdom eyes are like a momentary flash of lightning. She is the one who arose from the opening stamens of the lotus face of the Lord of the Three Worlds—the subterranean realm of the lower states, the terrestrial realm of humans, and the celestial realm of the higher states—the *Saṃbhogakāya* Avalokiteśvara. From that lotus face, which is like a blooming water-born flower, and from the stamens of those eyes, there arose the ocean of tears of compassion for beings, and from within the lotus that swirled from the right and left, she appeared as the white and blue Tārā, born by transformation, having pledged to be a companion in liberating beings. "To her, I offer homage"—apply this likewise to those that follow.

*Oṃ* is the introductory syllable. Because she has become the supreme mother of all the victorious ones, the Venerable Lady is exalted above the level of ordinary beings, and thus she is the Noble Lady (*Ārya*). Because she liberates those who have faith from cyclic existence, the lower realms, and fears, she is the Savior (*Tārā*); thus, "Homage to Tārā." This is the translator's homage. To whom is the homage paid? *Tāre* is the Savior; because she accomplishes [tasks] in an instant or in a single day, she is the Heroine who is swifter in her enlightened activity than other deities and who quickly turns back obstacles. *Tuttāre* is she who dispels fears. *Ture* is the Savior who grants all benefits—one's own, others', and the ultimate goal. The syllable *Svāhā* means "I bow to you." It appears that this is a blessed [verse] that arose in the manner of a summary of Tārā, which is renowned as having been supplemented from other tantras by the glorious Jowo Rje and others.

heading: གཉིས་པ་བསྟོད་པ་དངོས།
translation: To whom is the homage paid? It is to that beautiful one who, in terms of the qualities of her body, is like a hundred full autumn moons gathered together, her face white, beautiful, and fully radiant. If one contemplates that she, who is blazing with the nectar-like light that is brilliantly emitted by the rays of light that are even greater than those of a thousand gathered stars, dissolves into oneself, filling and stabilizing one's body, one will attain the *siddhi* of longevity and wisdom.

It is to that Savior who, through her wisdom, liberates those with faith from all fears; who, out of love for the one offering praise, does not delay even for an instant in her enlightened activity, and is thus the "Swift" one of compassion; and who, being capable, is the "Heroine" because she is certain of her ability to protect from all the fears of cyclic existence and peace. From that lotus face, which is like a blooming water-born flower, and from the stamens of those eyes, there arose the ocean of tears of compassion for beings, and from within the lotus that swirled from the right and left, she appeared as the white and blue Tārā, born by transformation, having pledged to be a companion in liberating beings. heading: གཉིས་པ་བསྟོད་པ་དངོས།
translation: Furthermore, to whom is the homage paid? It is to that delightful one whose left hand is beautifully adorned with a lotus that has grown from the water, possessing blue petals and stamens of a reddish-yellow golden hue, and which is a lotus stalk that is free from aging and decay, complete with leaves and fruit. Because she makes the six perfections—the causes of buddhahood, namely the perfection of generosity, diligence, austerity (which is ethical discipline), the wisdom of peace, patience, and meditative concentration—her sphere of activity, she is the one who acts in the manner of a *Bodhisattva* and a daughter of the Victorious Ones.

To whom is the homage paid? It is to that Savior who, through her wisdom, liberates those with faith from all fears; who, out of love for the one offering praise, does not delay even for an instant in her enlightened activity, and is thus the "Swift" one of compassion; and who, being capable, is the "Heroine" because she is certain of her ability to protect from all the fears of cyclic existence and peace. In her wrathful aspect, her wisdom eyes are like a momentary flash of lightning. She is the one who arose from the opening stamens of the lotus face of the Lord of the Three Worlds—the subterranean realm of the lower states, the terrestrial realm of humans, and the celestial realm of the higher states—the *Saṃbhogakāya* Avalokiteśvara. From that lotus face, which is like a blooming water-born flower, and from the stamens of those eyes, there arose the ocean of tears of compassion for beings, and from within the lotus that swirled from the right and left, she appeared as the white and blue Tārā, born by transformation, having pledged to be a companion in liberating beings. "To her, I offer homage"—apply this likewise to those that follow.

heading: གཉིས་པ་བསྟོད་པ་དངོས།
translation: Furthermore, to whom is the homage paid? It is to the one who is the jewel of the *uṣṇīṣa* of the assembly of the five families of the Victorious Ones, the Tathāgatas of the ten directions; who is the sovereign of the families, having been empowered as the infinite crown ornament; and who, because she is the one who acts in the manner of being victorious over all directions as if she were superior even to the Victorious Ones themselves, is the one who is most respectfully relied upon by the assemblies of the sons of the Victorious Ones—the *Bodhisattvas* who have attained the ten perfections in sequence throughout the world-realms of the ten directions—as the Mother who generates the wisdom of the path of seeing, the Mother who nurtures the wisdom of the path of meditation, and the Mother who always fulfills the aspirations of the path of no-more-learning and the rest.

heading: གཉིས་པ་བསྟོད་པ་དངོས།
translation: Furthermore, to whom is the homage paid? It is to the one who, by performing the application of the syllables *oṃ tuttāre hūṃ*, and relying upon the deity, mantra, and *samādhi* of the red Tārā, is able to summon—having trampled with her compassionate feet the great ones of the seven worlds, including the desire realm, the form realm, the formless realm, the space that fills them, and the six classes of beings along with the *antarābhava*—by bringing them under her power without exception.

heading: གཉིས་པ་བསྟོད་པ་དངོས།
translation: Furthermore, to whom is the homage paid? It is to the one who is worshipped with reverence even by the particles of dust at her feet by the ten guardians of the directions, headed by the great gods such as the great lord Maheśvara—who acts as the father even to the great protectors bearing various names, such as Indra, the greatest among the thirty-three; the fire deity Agni, the greatest among the sages; Brahmā, the greatest in the form realm; and the wind deity Vāyu, who is able to shake the three realms. Furthermore, it is to the one who is praised from before, with fear and trembling reverence, by hosts of such beings who are peerless in their greatness and power, including the *bhūtas* such as the Lord of Hosts (Gaṇapati), the *vetālas* such as the terrifying black one, the *gandharvas* such as the king of *gandharvas* Druma and those with horse-heads, and the *yakṣas* such as Vaiśravaṇa. If one pays homage to her, one will be free from the fear of those beings, both now and in all lifetimes to come.

It is to the one who is worshipped with reverence even by the particles of dust at her feet by the ten guardians of the directions, headed by the great gods such as the great lord Maheśvara—who acts as the father even to the great protectors bearing various names, such as Indra, the greatest among the thirty-three; the fire deity Agni, the greatest among the sages; Brahmā, the greatest in the form realm; and the wind deity Vāyu, who is able to shake the three realms. If one pays homage to her, one will be free from the fear of those beings, both now and in all lifetimes to come.

heading: གཉིས་པ་བསྟོད་པ་དངོས།
translation: Furthermore, to whom is the homage paid? It is to the one who, by the great and fearsome power of the deity mantra *oṃ ture svāhā*, instantly destroys all the champions of Māra and their retinues who manifest as the four Māras to cause one harm. Because she makes her face, which resembles a blooming water-born lotus, appear with a frowning expression, she is the one who, without even needing to be specifically invoked, naturally slays all the enemies of the practitioner who takes Tārā as their yidam, just as the sun dries the dew on the tip of a blade of grass.

heading: གཉིས་པ་བསྟོད་པ་དངོས།
translation: Furthermore, to whom is the homage paid? It is to the one who is completely filled with the supreme joy of an internal, stainless mental continuum, and who, on her external body, radiates splendor. She is the one who, even with the garlands of light from her precious crown, captivates and brings under her power all that is stationary and moving, cyclic existence and nirvana, and who spreads this delight. By the power of the *vidyā-mantra* *tuttāre*, she laughs with the laughter of speech to bring the world of cyclic existence under her power, and she laughs supremely to bring the supramundane world under her power. She is the one who, possessing the strength to subjugate the three realms, brings all demons and the world, both great and small, under her power, and thereby causes them to ripen and be liberated.

heading: གཉིས་པ་བསྟོད་པ་དངོས།
translation: Furthermore, to whom is the homage paid? It is to the one who has the power to summon all the sentient beings who protect the earth, and in particular, the hosts of human kings, as they all have faith in you. By the power and strength of gathering and dissolving—emanating from the countless hosts of the syllable *hūṃ*, which is the source of all desired attainments, along with light rays and the blessings of nectar, all while she moves her frowning expression in a wrathful manner—she is the one who completely liberates the practitioner from all destitution regarding Dharma, material wealth, physical form, and the sense fields.

translation: Furthermore, to whom is the homage paid? It is to the noble lady, the great mother of the expanse of the dharmakāya, the peaceful one who establishes beings in the happiness of the higher realms, the virtuous one who establishes them in liberation, and the one who establishes them in omniscience, whose very sphere of experience is the realization of the peace of nirvana in a single lifetime. By reciting her essence, the vidyā-mantra TĀRE TUTTĀRE—which is perfectly endowed with SVĀHĀ at the end and OṂ at the beginning—ten thousand, one hundred thousand, ten million, or one hundred million times, one destroys all the causes, such as the ten non-virtuous acts and the five heinous crimes, and all the results, such as the suffering of illness, demonic interference, and physical pain, as well as the fears of mental derangement, agitation, and fainting; she is the one who performs the activity of pacification.

heading: གཉིས་པ་བསྟོད་པ་དངོས།
translation: Furthermore, to whom is the homage paid? It is to you, the goddess who delights in being surrounded by an assembly of vidyādharas, realized beings, and bodhisattva heirs, and who shatters the bodies of enemies by scattering them into pieces. It is to the very Tārā who is generated from the HŪṂ of the essence and the seed syllable that generates the vidyā-mantra, upon whose speech the ten-syllable mantra of the wrathful Tārā is arranged.

heading: གཉིས་པ་བསྟོད་པ་དངོས།
translation: Furthermore, to whom is the homage paid? It is to the Ture, the Tārā who, by manifesting the miraculous display of her form, stamps her feet upon the ground, which is like Mount Meru, the king of mountains, and the continents. She is the one whose essence is the seed-syllable in the form of Hūṃ, which is the cause for generating you, the wrathful one, and the life-force of your heart. She is the one who, by shaking the three realms—the subterranean world of the lower realms, the terrestrial world of humans, and the celestial world of the higher realms—through the ten types of earth-shaking, suppresses and overcomes all that is cruel and harsh, including Mount Meru, the king of mountains at the center, the mountains Mandara and Vindhya that reside within the surrounding oceans where the gods and great sages dwell.

Furthermore, to whom is the homage paid? It is to the noble lady, the great mother of the expanse of the dharmakāya, the peaceful one who establishes beings in the happiness of the higher realms, the virtuous one who establishes them in liberation, and the one who establishes them in omniscience, whose very sphere of experience is the realization of the peace of nirvana in a single lifetime. translation: Furthermore, to whom is the homage paid? It is to Tārā, who possesses eyes as brilliant as the full sun and moon—the right eye, like the sun, having rays of fire that burn away all enemies, obstructors, illnesses, demonic spirits, and obscurations, and the left eye, like the moon, having rays of nectar that increase all lifespan, wisdom, and merit—and who is the one endowed with such eyes of supreme radiance. Furthermore, to whom is the homage paid? It is to Tārā, who possesses eyes as brilliant as the full sun and moon—the right eye, like the sun, having rays of fire that burn away all enemies, obstructors, illnesses, demonic spirits, and obscurations, and the left eye, like the moon, having rays of nectar that increase all lifespan, wisdom, and merit—and who is the one endowed with such eyes of supreme radiance. Having meditated upon her in the sky before oneself or performed the self-generation, one should recite the mantra *oṃ hara hara tuttāre svāhā*. As indicated by the literal meaning of the mantra, by reciting the two *hara*s and *tuttāre*, she is the one who dispels extremely violent epidemics and contagious diseases, such as earth-anthrax, sky-anthrax, smallpox, virulent fevers, heat fevers, bilious fevers, and common colds, as well as other illnesses of heat, cold, and combined disorders arising from past karma or immediate conditions, and in particular, she is the one who pacifies previously contracted epidemic diseases and prevents them from arising in the future.

Work: པདྨ་རྣམ་རྒྱལ་གྱི་སྒྲོལ་མའི་བསྟོད་འགྲེལ། (author: Ldombuwa Pema Namgyal). A canonical Tibetan text; the blocks below are being translated one at a time, in order.

Preceding blocks of this same document and their translations — match this terminology, register and line shape:

[1-29] source:
གཞན་ཡང་སྦས་དོན་ལྟར་ན། རལ་པའི་ཁྲོད་ན་འོད་དཔག་མེད་ཀྱིས་བུམ་དབང་དང༌། ཟླ་བའི་དུམ་བུས་དབུ་རྒྱན་ཅེས་པས་ཐིག་ལེ་འདྲེན་པའི་གསང་དབང་དང་། བདེ་མ། དགེ་མ། ཞི་མ། མྱ་ངན་འདས་ཞི་བཞི་པོས། ཤེར་དབང་གི་དབང་བཞི་དང་། དེ་ཉིད་གསུམ་གྱིས་རྣམ་ཐར་གསུམ་ལྡན་གྱི་དབང་བཞི་པ་དང༌། དབུ་རྒྱན་འོད་ཀྱི་ཕྲེང་བ་སྤེལ་མ་ཞེས་པས་ཅོད་པན་བསྟན་པ་སོགས་དབང་གི་དོན་དང༌། ཀུན་ནས་བསྐོར་རབ་དགའ་བ་དང་། གཡས་བརྐྱང་གཡོན་བསྐུམ་ཀུན་ནས་བསྐོར་དགའི་ཞེས་པས་གཙོ་འཁོར་བསྐྱེད་རིམ་ཕྱོགས་དང་ཉི་མ་ཟླ་བ་སོགས་ཀྱི་ཐིག་རླུང་རྫོགས་རིམ་ཕྱོགས་ནས་བསྟན་ཚུལ་ལྟར་རྒྱས་པར་འགྲེལ་ནུས་ཀྱང་དེ་དག་ནི་རྒྱུད་གཞན་ནས་རྫོགས་པར་བསྟན་པས། རྒྱུད་ཚིག་ཉུང་ངུའི་སྐབས་འདིར་ནི་དངོས་བསྟན་གྱི་སྙིང་པོ་རྙོག་པ་མེད་པ་དྭངས་སི་ལེ་ལེན་པར་འདོད་དེ་བཀྲོལ་བ་ཡིན་ནོ། །
[1-29] translation already produced for this document:
Furthermore, according to the hidden meaning: "Amidst the matted hair, Amitābha" refers to the vase empowerment; "a crescent moon as a diadem" refers to the secret empowerment of drawing the *bindu*; the four—*bdemā*, *dgemā*, *zhimā*, and *mya ngan 'das zhi*—refer to the four empowerments of the wisdom-knowledge empowerment; the three suchnesses refer to the fourth empowerment, which possesses the three liberations; and "a diadem of light garlands" refers to the crown ornament and other meanings of empowerment. Moreover, "circling in all directions, supreme joy" and "right leg extended, left drawn in, circling in all directions with joy" refer to the generation stage of the principal deity and retinue, and the way of teaching the completion stage through the *bindu* and *prāṇa* of the sun, moon, and so forth. Although these could be explained in great detail, since they are taught completely in other tantras, in this context of a concise tantric text, I have chosen to extract only the clear, unclouded essence of the direct meaning and have explained it accordingly.

[1-30] source:
རྒྱུད་འདིའི་བསྟན་དོན་རྒྱས་ན། སྒྲོལ་མ་ཉིན་ཞི་མཚན་ཁྲོའི་སྒྲུབ་ཐབས་དང་། སྒྲུབ་ཐབས་ཉེར་གཅིག་དང་ལས་ཚོགས་ཉེར་གཅིག་རྣམས་ཀྱང་བསྟན་པ་ཡིན་ནོ། །དེས་དངོས་གཞི་བསྟོད་པའི་དོན་སོང༌།
[1-30] translation already produced for this document:
If the meaning taught in this tantra is expanded, it also reveals the *sādhana* of Tārā as peaceful by day and wrathful by night, the twenty-one *sādhanas*, and the twenty-one ritual activities. With this, the meaning of the actual praise is concluded.

heading: གསུམ་པ་མཇུག་ཕན་ཡོན།
translation: For any intelligent person who possesses genuine devotion to the Goddess, the object of praise, by reciting the tantric words of praise with a mind that is thoroughly purified in the manner of praising,

heading: གསུམ་པ་མཇུག་ཕན་ཡོན།
translation: The time for praise is at dusk, when spirits and demons, who are inclined toward darkness, cause harm, and at dawn, the time when the gods give prophecies; one should rise from bed and, by merely recollecting the Noble One, be granted all power of fearlessness and confidence. The cause, all misdeeds, is thoroughly pacified, and the result—sickness, demons, misfortune, bad omens, and the doors of birth into the three lower realms—is blocked, thereby destroying all miserable rebirths.

translation:
According to the intentions of sentient beings,
And their various levels of mental capacity,
I pray you turn the wheel of Dharma of the Great Vehicle (the Bodhisattva vehicle of both Sūtra and Tantra), the Small Vehicle (the two vehicles of Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas), and the Common Vehicle (the two vehicles of gods and humans of the higher realms).
I beseech you to turn the wheel of Dharma.
